headline: Recommended Planning Board approval of 52 Locke Rd and 270 Loudon Rd projects; continued 7 Rectory Rd to November 10th.
summary: A public hearing was held on a request to discontinue part of the West End Farm Trail at 74 Currier Rd. Members will deliberate and decide at a later meeting. Members also approved a memorial bench at Winant Park, approved keeping existing signs on a donated parcel, and approved minutes of the September 9, 2026 meeting.
decisions: Approved the September 9, 2026 meeting minutes as amended to correct the spelling of "Bowser".
Approved acceptance of funding and installation of a memorial bench at Winant Park, funded by Jennifer Goodman.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the CUP application at 52 Locke Rd as submitted, 5-0 with Vice-Chair Lewis recused.
Continued the Planning Board CUP application for 7 Rectory Rd to November 10th.
Recommended that the Planning Board approve the site plan application at 270 Loudon Rd as submitted.
Approved nominating Member Lesser as regular member and Alternate Member Currie as alternate member for the Planning Board Advisory master plan work.
Approved keeping the existing signs on the Bois De Brodeur parcel.

decision_evidence.quote: Member Coen moved, Member Chormann seconded, to approve the September 9, 2026 as amended correcting the spelling of “Bowser”. All in favor. The motion passed.

On a motion made by Member Porter, seconded by Vice Chair Lewis, the Conservation Commission voted to approve the acceptance of funding and installation of a memorial bench. All in favor. The motion passed.
Member Coen moved, Member Porter seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve as submitted. All in favor. The motion passed.
c. Planning Board CUP (2026-091)- 7 Rectory Rd (Continued to November 10th)
Member Coen moved, Vice-Chair Lewis seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve as submitted. All in favor. The motion passed.

Vice-Chair Lewis made a motion to nominate Member Lesser to be a regular member and Alternate Member Currie as an alternate member for the Planning Board Advisory. Member Porter seconded. All in favor. The motion passed.
Member Lesser moved, Member Chormann seconded, to approve keeping the existing signs on the property. All in favor. The motion passed.

CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
1 
 
Attendees:      Chair Kristine Tardiff, Vice-Chair Jeff Lewis, Kevin Porter, Alternate Jim 
Owers, Rick Chormann, Mark Coen, Councilor Michele Horne, Tracey Lesser 
and Alternate Member Bruce Currie 
 
Absent:  Katherine Healy 
 
Staff:   Kearsten O’Brien, Senior Planner 
  Alec Bass, Assistant City Planner - Community 
  Krista Tremblay, Administrative Technician III 
     
Public:  Ron Klemarczyk, contracted City Forester  
  
  
  
1. Call to Order 
The meeting was called to order by Chair Tardiff at 7:00 p.m.  
 
2. Minutes – Approve meeting minutes from meeting on September 9,2026 
Member Coen moved, Member Chormann seconded, to approve the September 9, 2026 as amended 
correcting the spelling of “Bowser”. All in favor. The motion passed. 
 
3. Public Hearing regarding the discontinuance of the portion of the West End Farm Trail located at 74 
Currier Rd. 
 
Chair Tardiff stated the Conservation Commission’s role is to gather and consider relevant information 
regarding the request to discontinue the WEFT portion of the trail at 74 Currier Rd and then come to a 
decision at a future meeting. At the time that the September public hearing was scheduled, the Marro’s 
had requested to continue the public hearing to October 14th as they were unable to attend the meeting. 
The Commission opened the public hearing for those who were able to attend to receive the public 
testimony and then, upon the advice of the City Solicitor’s office, the commission moved and voted to 
continue the public hearing to a date certain of October 14th. 
 
The Trails Subcommittee adopted Procedural Guidelines for Discontinuance of a Trail or Trail Network. 
This is not a formal policy of the City of Concord, but a decision-making tool to assist with 
recommendations to the Conservation Commission. At the July 8 meeting, the Trails Subcommittee 
completed their information-gathering portion of the review process outlined in the Guidelines. At the 
August 12th Trails Subcommittee meeting the Subcommittee deliberated and made a recommendation to 
the Conservation Commission. The recommendation from the Trails Subcommittee is linked to the 
Conservation Commission agenda for this evenings meeting. 
 
The purpose of today’s agenda item is conducting a public hearing to receive further public testimony 
regarding the request to discontinue the portion of the WEFT located at 74 Currier road. The 
Conservation Commission will consider the public testimony along with the information gathered by the
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
2 
 
Trails Subcommittee before taking any final action on the request. 
 
Chair Tardiff also emphasized that the Commission is not making the final decision regarding 
discontinuance of the West End Farm Trail until after the required public hearing is completed, and the 
Commission makes their final decision, which will not occur until a future meeting. Members of the 
Public will have 5 minutes to testify. Chair Tardiff stated that she will allow the Marro’s additional time 
to give their testimony. Chair Tardiff read in testimony sent in from members of the public attached to the 
end of the meeting minutes. 
 
Chair Tardiff opened the public hearing at 7:06 PM.  
 
Mr. Marro of 76 Currier Rd, thanked the Conservation Commission for allowing them to be here and 
introduced his wife Beth Marro and their three dogs. Mr. and Mrs. Marro stated they brought three of 
their dogs that people are claiming attack people along the trail. Mrs. Marro stated that the dogs are 
therapy dogs and work with children with autism, elderly and people with disabilities. They wanted the 
public to see how the dogs behave. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that he is here tonight to ask the Commission to seriously consider discontinuing or 
relocating the trail immediately behind their property. Mr. Marro stated in the past he never asked to close 
the section, and that he asked to close the parking lot. Mr. Marro stated that they requested to close the 
trial if the City of Concord was unable to offer mitigating or some sort of solutions to the problems. Mr. 
Marro stated since 2019 they have been dealing with the City through his attorney to the City’s Solicitors 
Office to try and come up with solutions to the problem and nothing has been done to this day. He stated 
that he has attended many meetings and City Council Member Stacey Brown can attest, that there was a 
list of things in place that the City Trail Subcommittee had to resolve and only two signs were put up 
stating the property is under Surveillance. Mr. Marro stated that they were supposed to put up hours of 
operation and stated there was discussion about a fence and putting a gate at the parking lot to limit the 
hours.  
 
Mr. Marro stated that for years they have evidence and showed pictures at the meeting of the problems 
taking place. Mr. Marro stated that he is asking that they consider rerouting or coming up with solutions 
to the problems. Mr. Marro stated that he is not in objection to trails or outdoor recreation at all, unlike 
what people have made him out to be. He stated that none of the people know the facts and are telling lies 
as written about him in testimonies. Mr. Marro asked the Commission if they could provide the date of 
when the City acquired the property. Alternate-Member Owers said 2010. Mrs. Marro asked if anyone on 
the Commission knew when Mr. Marro purchased the house. Alternate-Member Owers stated 2003 and 
there was already a trail on the property.  
 
Mr. Marro stated that yes there was a snowmobile trail that was by kind permission of land owners. The 
trail traveled through the Marro’s property. Mr. Marro stated that in 2019 after being unable to negotiate 
with City through his attorney, had shut down the section of the trail that was on his property, as his right
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
3 
 
as a landowner. Mr. Marro asked that people who are landowners think about how they would feel if they 
had a trail on their property without permission that the City had brought in heavy equipment to widen the 
trail, without permission. Mr. Marro stated that he had tried to negotiate with the City and the City wanted 
nothing to do with it and they were done. Mr. Marro said that he would like to correct the record that he 
did close the portion of the trail down that went through his property.  
 
Mr. Marro stated that he did purchase the property in 2003 and this matter has managed to divide his 
neighbors and himself and they have been friends for 21 years. He stated that he has always been a good 
neighbor he would plow their driveway when they were away, without them asking. Mr. Marro stated the 
City acquired the land in 2010 there was an established snowmobile trail that was allowed by the 
landowners. In the past the Snowmobile club would come to him and it was never a problem until last 
year. Mr. Marro stated that some of the public comment states that they moved to the property know that 
they knew there was a trail there prior to them purchasing the property and that is incorrect, he purchased 
it prior to the trail being there. Mr. Marro stated that he is asking the Conservation Commission to 
examine the underlying records rather than to assume the present route was properly evaluated from the 
beginning. Mr. Marro stated that they are the only home on that section of the trail. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that there are signs in place that specifically state that there are no motorized vehicles on 
the property. Mr. Marro stated there are no exclusions allowing for certain people to drive on the trail. Mr. 
Marro stated there are private vehicles that drive up and down the trail such as the snowmobile club, 
people contracted through the city and, people on motorized bicycles. Mr. Marro stated they have found 
litter, unleashed dogs and yes dogs can be off leash on conservation land but it also states to respect land 
owners and to put their dogs on a leash while walking by homes. He stated that many people do not do 
that and they have had dogs run into their yard. Mrs. Marro stated that one of their dogs have been 
attacked by another dog not on a leash and it had been documented with the vet and police. Mr. Marro 
stated the police were unable to help after a response time of 4 hours. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that people are suggesting that they have their dogs on leashes, but it is ok for people 
walking the trail to have their dogs off leash while walking on the trail and that is nonsense. Mr. Marro 
stated that yes, his dogs bark while people walk the trail. He stated that most people know if they own a 
dog that yes dogs bark when somebody is in your front or back yard. He stated that people take pictures 
of his house while walking on the trail. Mrs. Marro stated that they had an incident today where she had 
to call the police because they were being harassed. Mr. Marro stated that at the July meeting he was 
allowed to speak and he had asked questions that were in regards to the City’s Trails Master Plan and how 
they handle issues on the trail. He stated that the Commission should have the questions. Mr. Marro stated 
that has never happened with them. Mrs. Marro stated that they were told they would have answers to 
their questions by August and they have never received them. Mr. Marro stated that when they were at the 
Trails Subcommittee meeting in August they were told they were not allowed to speak and it was not 
open for public comment. Mr. Marro stated that at the Trails Subcommittee a member of the 
subcommittee had raised his hand and said this is one of Concord’s most beloved trails and is a heavily 
used trail and I love the overlook and who agrees with me. Mr. Marro stated that one of the other
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
4 
 
members of the trail’s subcommittee stated that they agreed that it is a heavily used trail. Mr. Marro said 
that he documented 31 days prior to that meeting of trail usages. He stated that he documented whether 
they were male or female users, if they had dogs and even documented other wildlife. Mr. Marro stated 
that he provided the data in an excel spread sheet and he also provided data regarding the parking lot. He 
stated that is it very rarely used as an area for to people to park using the trail. He stated it is mainly an 
area for people to hang out and for people to turn around in. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that not one of the commission members or City Council members or Councilor’s -At-
Large members who said they would communicate with him and never heard from them again. Chair 
Tardiff stated that the only question before the Commission tonight is the trail and that she understands 
the parking lot is linked to the trail but they are discussing the discontinuance of the trail. Mr. Marro 
stated that he provided 31 days of data regarding the trail and the City has not provided any regarding 
their claims regarding most beloved trail. Mr. Marro said that this is their sanctuary and yes, they are 
angry and upset tonight, not only in how they have been treated but also in how they have been portrayed 
in social media and newspaper. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that a gentleman by the name of Sam Evans-Brown who wrote a letter to the editor. 
Chair Tardiff stated that the letters to the editor are not part testimony. Mr. and Mrs. Marro stated it is 
because this is where people are getting their information about them from. Especially people who do not 
live in the city have been allowed to speak and submit testimony. Mrs. Marro asked why the commission 
is considering their testimony when they do not even reside here. Chair Tardiff stated this is a public 
hearing and anyone here can testify and ask where people are from. Mr. Marro said he brings up Sam 
Evans- Brown because he wrote something and published it the Concord Monitor that is not factual and 
essentially lies and people took that and wrote letters to the commission and posted on social media to 
jump on the band wagon to be against them. Mr. Marro asked what the policy was regarding receiving 
comments from people who do not reside in Concord.  
 
Chair Tardiff stated that the City may have one and at meetings she has been to at the City people are 
allowed to come through and testify and are asked to identify where they are from. Chair Tardiff stated 
that the Commission will not be excluding public testimony. Councilor Horne stated that they do allow 
public testimony of non- residents because they work, recreate, etc. and are allowed to testify. Mr. Marro 
asked if she was 100% sure that is with in the City’s rules. Councilor Horne stated yes.  Mr. Marro asked 
Councilor Horne to provide him that information in writing. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that where the City is failing is that he began by asking the City to close the parking lot. 
He stated that where it became a trail problem is more on the City than him. Mr. Marro stated that if the 
City can not properly maintain and control what goes on, on the trail or in the parking lot then to do 
something about or close it. Mr. Marro presented the commission during his testimony pictures of misuse 
on the trail such as people using the parking lot and his property as a bathroom, teenagers and adults 
giving his camera the middle finger, vehicles driving up the trail, a person releasing an animal on the trail, 
litter, people attaching political signs to their vehicles and facing them towards his property, litter of sex
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
5 
 
toys, bikes using the trail where it states no bikes allowed. Mr. Marro stated that there are signs that say 
no bikes allowed without written permission by the landowners, and yet there are people using with trail 
with bikes. Mrs. Marro stated that because of the commission they are being harassed by people using the 
trail. Mrs. Marro stated that at the last meeting someone suggested using bear spray, and if anyone uses 
bear spray on their dogs they will hear about it. Mr. Marro stated that they are looked as monsters of the 
neighborhood. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that according to Ms. Ross no one is allowed to ride on their property and she stated that 
for him this evening. Member Coen stated that he thinks that the Marro’s have made their point and 
would like to know their recommendation of what they would like to see. Mr. Marro stated if you can not 
enforce the law or monitor it then either reroute it and if you can not reroute it then close that portion of 
the WEFT down. Mr. Marro stated he would like to see hours of operation enforceable and a gate on the 
parking lot to prevent vehicles and illegal activity from happening in the parking lot after hours. Mr. 
Marro stated he asked for a fence years ago. Member Coen asked if Mr. Marro was allowed to put up a 
fence. Mrs. Marro stated why should they have to pay for it, they were there first so they shouldn’t have 
to. Mr. Marro stated he isn’t the bad neighbor but yes, he could. Member. Coen went over the 
recommendations of the Marro’s to resolve the issues, they would like a gate at the parking lot and hours 
of operation that are enforceable, to either reroute the trail if the city can not enforce or monitor the trail 
and if they can not to discontinue the trail. Mr. Marro stated that is correct and he would like to see fence 
be put up in that section to prevent people from looking into their property and from dogs wandering onto 
their property. Member Coen thanked them for testifying. 
 
Mr. Marro stated that he talked a little about the trails plan that the commission has not followed, proven 
to follow, and have not answered the questions I asked. He asked the commission to answer the questions 
and was promised them. Mr. Marro stated the Trails Subcommittee has created situations where if you are 
friends with them or bike member buddies with them you can speak, but if a member of the public tries to 
speak you are shut down. Mr. Marro stated that is not okay it is a double standard and is not acceptable. 
He stated that at the September trails meeting a member of a bike club was allowed to speak but the 
month prior when he tried to speak he was shut down. Alternate Member Owers asked for a picture of his 
house from the trail because he is trying to envision where the fence would go. Mr. Marro stated the trail 
would be best placed along the trail because you would need to cut down the trees. 
 
Chair Tardiff asked the Marro’s if their request for fencing was along the whole boundary. The Marro’s 
said yes along the whole boundary. Chair Tardiff asked if they are looking for visual barriers. Mr. Marro 
said it could be visual for all the looky-loos or people who like to take pictures and said the rest of it can 
be a simple chicken wire fence. Mr. Marro said he contacted the people who sent in letters to speak with 
him and talk to him about the issues he is facing and not one of them contacted him. Mr. Marro said that 
it appears that there is a conflict of interest of members of the trails subcommittee who are part of 
NEMBA and State Nine Racing. Mr. Marro stated these are people who should be excluding themselves 
from recommendations when the recommendations benefit them. Mr. Marro said there should be an 
honest look of these members and asked the commission to look into the members. Mr. Marro stated that
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION

October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
6 
 
he wants peace and quiet for all. 
 
Ron Klemarzyk the City’s consulting Forester clarified a few things, he said the subdivision survey from 
when the subdivision occurred showed the trail on the property when the city acquired it. The City then 
surveyed to make sure the boundaries were correct and they were not. The city then corrected the issue 
and relocated the trail off the property. Mr. Klemarzyk stated there are signs out there that say no bicycles 
but those are on the Rossview property and what he understands is that bicycles are allowed all the way 
from District #5 Rd all the way down to Currier Rd. The split rail fence was donated by the abutter of the 
Rossview property and that is not the property line the property line for the Rossview property is an old 
fence that was blazed by the surveyor who surveyed the property for the conservation easement. The 
Sewalls Falls property is State property and that is why there is hours of operation at that site. 
 
Boyd Smith of 139 Liberty St, came to testify in favor of keeping the trail. Mr. Smith stated that he has 
been using the trail for about 20 years or so and has beautiful natural resources. Mr. Smith stated he heard 
their concerns regarding misuse of the trail and respect their right to enjoy their property. There are some 
enforcement issues that need to be monitored by the City and he understands that can be a burden to the 
city. Mr. Smith stated if the land is owned by the City we should use it as a trail and take care of it. The 
trail system in Concord is remarkable and we can not have the issues they discussed taking place and that 
is something that should be taken care of and we should not close the trail down. 
 
Scott Betournay said he resides in Concord and said he loves the WEFT and there is a wonderful view 
that looks over a pond that he likes to run and walk to and would appreciate the trail staying open. 
 
Stephen Murray a resident of Concord said that he has walked that trail hundreds of times and he has been 
harassed by their dogs while walking his dog. Mr. Murray said the dogs that harassed him were not the 
ones that attended the meeting so either those are props or they are new dogs. Mr. Murray said it is a great 
trail and being bullied by the people to close the trail is inappropriate.  
 
Sean Reese of 35 Timberline Dr stated Concord has many trails and this portion of the trail is not the only 
portion that people litter or are vagrants, that occurs across the City. Mr. Reese stated that the City should 
consider how those issues are handled at other areas that are similar. Mr. Reese said that it is his 
understanding that we don’t go directly for shutting down a trail when a compliant comes through. He 
stated that the City should not exceed to the land owner because it will set a precedent to other property 
owners who abut trails. 
 
Kate Kellenier of 126 South St state that she walks her dog there and would hate for it to be shut down. 
She hopes that we can find some common ground. 
 
Roland Berube of 8 Spaulding St, said that he has a lot of sympathy for the Marro’s hearing them attest to 
what they go through. He can not personally attest that is what they go through and has to take their word 
for what they say. Mr. Berube said as a person who uses that trail he needs that parking lot and it is
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION

October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
7 
 
inconvenient because he would have to park on the side of the road. He likes to snowshoe out onto the 
ponds because they are frozen at that point. He is glad the city mitigated the issue of the trail being on his 
property. Mr. Berube said he cannot condone or stop other hikers or bikers from the use of the trail. Mr. 
Berube said that he was the trail administrator for the Bow Pioneers and it is an important corridor for 
snowmobilers to travel. He would hate for the trail to be closed and that opportunity to go away as well. 
Mr. Berube said he has not seen trash or vagrants using the trial. He can speak to the signs as you see 
when you park in the parking lot and he said that there is a political sign posted from their property and 
some of the people could be responding to that. Mr. Berube asked that the City work with them to get 
their privacy back and not close the trail. 
 
Chair Tardiff closed the public hearing. 
 
Chair Tardiff said they are not going to deliberate tonight and will discuss at their November meeting and 
take all testimony into consideration. 
 
4. New Business 
a. Memorial Bench -Jennifer Goodman 
Ms. O’Brien stated this was brought before the Commission. It was then deferred to the Trails 
Subcommittee and they had a discussion. The consensus after discussion with the city forester 
that there is a bench at Winant Park that needs to be replaced. The proposal is that Jennifer 
Goodman will cover the cost of the new bench. If the Commission is ok with that a motion and 
vote would be needed to proceed. Then Ms. O’Brien will notify Jennifer Goodman that she can 
move forward with the bench.  
 
Chair Tardiff noted for the Commission they have had prior discussion on the bench. 
 
On a motion made by Member Porter, seconded by Vice Chair Lewis, the Conservation 
Commission voted to approve the acceptance of funding and installation of a memorial bench. 
All in favor. The motion passed.  
 
b. Planning Board CUP (2026-087)- 52 Locke Rd 
Vice-Chair Lewis recused due to conflict with work. 
 
Randal Shuey (119 Storrs St, Concord) is present to represent this application. Mr. Shuey 
presented a restoration plan for wetland buffer that was logged in 2025. Mr. Shuey noted they 
were before the Commission in April to discuss the restoration plan for the buffer in 
conjunction with a flexible development of industrial and warehouse storage. The developer 
has since decided to do a micro data center. The center of the property at the end of Locke Rd 
there is an existing gravel road that goes onto the adjacent property that leads for a cell tower. 
This is on undeveloped land. The owner of the property had it logged down to wetland 
boundary. Which was flagged prior to them doing their work. The owner was notified by
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
8 
 
Northpoint Engineering that the city has a 50-foot buffer off the wetland and as a part of the 
plan they will need to come up with a restoration plan. Mr. Shuey presented the existing 
condition and to the north it is flat with a couple stock piles. The south side of the road has a 
little steeper slope. There is a wetland on both the north and south sides of the road. The south 
side of the road is a forested wetland. The north side is scrub and shrub wetland. When were 
before the Commission in April there is a little wetland impact on the southern side line. On 
Locke Road there is a drainage ditch and they have drawn a 50-foot buffer around that. The 
current plan has the entire southern side of the road being undeveloped. They have submitted a 
detailed planting plan to restore the buffer.    
 
Chair Tardiff asked on the restoration land that is consistent with the conversation in April. 
Chair Tardiff asked aside from the restoration are there other impacts to the wetland buffer 
from the retention basin.  
 
Mr. Shuey stated all of the grading for the project is outside of the 50-foot buffer.  
 
Mr. Bass noted the emergency over flow spillway of one of the retention pond would lead in 
that area.  
 
Member Lesser raised a question about the emergency spill way on the storm water retention 
basin and asked if that is cooling water from the data center or just surface water and run off 
from the roofs and parking.  
 
Mr. Shuey stated that is not a cooling water retention pond it is a storm water pond.  
 
Chair Tardiff noted it appears to function like a storm water retention basin.  
 
Mr. Shuey noted that part of the property on the northern side has good sand and filtration. 
 
Member Coen moved, Member Porter seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve as 
submitted. All in favor. The motion passed. 
 
Vice-Chair Lewis arrived back in the room as a voting member.  
 
c. Planning Board CUP (2026-091)- 7 Rectory Rd (Continued to November 10th) 
 
d. Planning Board CUP (2026-092)- 270 Loudon Rd 
Huston Hubbard (100 Domain Dr Ste 201, Exeter) and Doug Richardson (40 Franklin St, 
Needham MA) are present to represent this application. Mr. Richardson stated this is the 
first site plan application for development on the northeast corner. There will be 110 units 
in a four-story building.
CONCORD CONSERVATION COMMISSION 
MEETING MINUTES- Draft 
October 14, 2026, 7:00 p.m. 
Council Chambers, 37 Green St 
 
9 
 
Mr. Hubbard stated this project will redevelop the existing parking lot as the malls snow 
dump area. Mr. Hubbard noted the project proposes roughly 1900 square feet of wetland 
buffer impact. The impact area will be revegetated. The reason for the buffer impact is they 
know the contractor will need to have space to get around the structure. The existing 
parking lot does provide some storm water collection, treatment and infiltration. The 
proposed storm water design has a closed drain system connect to a hydrodynamic 
separator. The water line will connect to the mall existing drainage system.   
 
Member Porter asked for explanation on the hydrodynamic separator.  
 
Mr. Hubbard stated it is used for pretreatment for the water they collect on site and will 
separate suspended solids of water to the infiltration system. Then that will go to the 
drainage system. The roof drains tie into the system.  
 
Chair Tardiff asked for clarity on the proposal is and asked if this will be a temporary 
impact to the buffer during construction.  
 
Mr. Hubbard replied yes, the intent is to restore and revegetate.  
  
Mr. Richardson pointed out there are no exterior doors on that side of the building. 
  
Chair Tardiff asked if there will be a path or access path for use.  
 
Mr. Hubbard noted there is a path on the east side of the building.  
 
Vice-Chair Lewis pointed out there is a sewer line with a sewer easement and that is 
downhill of the proposed impact.  
Member Coen moved, Vice-Chair Lewis seconded, to recommend the Planning Board approve 
as submitted. All in favor. The motion passed.

Oct. 12, 2026 
Dear Concord Conservation Commission members, 
I am writing to update my opposition to closing the West End Farm Trail (WEFT) and parking lot 
north of Currier Road. I attended the Commission’s Sept. 9 hearing and was surprised that every 
speaker (as well as those who have submitted written comments to date), with the exception of 
City Councilor Stacey Brown, not only opposed the closure, but sounded some familiar, 
troubling themes. 
I have since reviewed meeting minutes, correspondence and comments from the Conservation 
Commission and Trails Subcommittee, as well as public records from the Concord Police, and 
have concluded that there simply is not enough evidence to justify closing this important trail 
access to the public. Key points: 
 
Opposition to a fence 
I no longer support a proposal to build a fence at the city’s expense along the abutting property 
of Rene Marro. This would set a costly precedent open to every abutter of a public trail or park 
in our city. At the Commission’s Feb. 11, 2026 meeting, Mr. Marro also said that a fence would 
not solve his issues with noise, or with loose dogs on his property. 
 
Public safety concerns, records:  A two-way street 
In January 2024, Rene Marro wrote to City Councilor Stacey Brown that, “What goes on 
regularly on this trail has literally made our home a miserable place to be,” noting that trail 
users frequently leave trash, create loud noise, allow their dogs to run loose onto his property 
and harass and attack his dogs, defecate and urinate on the trail, have sex in the parking lot, 
leave trash, and invade his privacy. Since the city put in the trail, he said it has become “overrun 
by degenerates, I loved where I live. Now not only do I hate it here, we are now no longer safe 
in our own home.” Obviously, these sorts of allegations and incidents are highly upsetting and 
intolerable. 
 
However, the public record shows a more nuanced situation, where Mr. Marro’s complaints are 
balanced out by complaints of trail users against him. 
 
Mr. Marro shared careful records of daily trail use from August this year, showing that 2 people 
a day using the trail on average. None caused trouble that resulted in police action or charges. 
That hardly qualiﬁes as “overrun by degenerates.”
From July 17 through Aug. 12 this year, he also recorded 53 visits to the parking lot, where 
people either stayed in their vehicles or used the lot to turn around. As someone who 
frequently uses Concord’s trails, this does not strike me as unusual at all, or cause for alarm. I 
often see people taking a break, eating lunch, reading, or listening to music in their cars at 
trailheads. 
 
I have visited the WEFT parking lot on Currier Road, Winant Trailhead on Fisk Road, and Swope 
Trailhead on Long Pond Road parking lots four times in the early morning since Sept. 9 and 
found negligible trash as Currier—and far more trash at Fisk and Swope (and much more along 
the roadsides between the trails). 
 
In addition to comments to the Commission, public records from the Concord Police 
Department from 2024, 2025 and through 2026 show that trail users have reported concerns 
with Marros’ dogs being loose, on the trail and acting aggressively. They also commented about 
guns frequently being ﬁred on the Marros’ gun range when trail users are nearby, which makes 
some trail users feel unsafe. In addition, the Bow Pioneers Snowmobile Club, a neighbor, and 
others complained that the trail and parking lot have been purposely blocked by snow and 
felled trees and limbs from the abutting property. 
 
Of the 16* records released by the Concord Police from the last 3 years, 10 were made by Rene 
Marro, including complaints of loose dogs, a young couple smoking pot, someone “acting 
weird,” people in a car doing drugs and leaving trash, and several people urinating or 
defecating. Over the same time, there were 7 reports made by trail users complaining of 
Marros’ loose dogs on the trail, safety concerns with his ﬁring range, and snow, felled trees or 
limbs blocking the trail. At your Sept. 9 meeting, more trail users shared complaints that they 
did not report to the police. 
 
Following up on one complaint made by Mr. Marro, the Concord Police contacted the 
Manchester Police to track down an older woman who was caught urinating on the trail by one 
of Mr. Marro’s cameras. The police tracked down her vehicle and identiﬁcation. The Manchester 
police contacted her and lectured her about the law regarding urinating in public, for which she 
apologized profusely. Surely, the woman had no idea she was being videotaped—and urinating 
in the woods and out of public view is undoubtedly very common. This investigation does not 
strike me as the best use of police time in Concord and Manchester. 
 
*The Concord PD withheld at least two records for privacy reasons and/or because an active 
investigation.
Winant Park Trailhead: A comparison 
In 2024, 2025 and through 2026, Concord Police records show no complaints either against or 
by the abutters of the Winant Park Trailhead, at 18 Fisk Road, involving the trail or parking lot. 
This, despite a small side-trail leading directing from the parking lot to the abutters’ home. 
 
Although no studies are available to compare trail use numbers between the Fisk and Currier 
parking lots, I believe the Fisk trailhead receives more use. I also believe that trail use of the 
WEFT has declined in recent years due to issues with Mr. Marro’s signage, dogs and shooting 
range, which were cited by several speakers at the Sept. 9 Conservation Commission meeting 
who now avoid the trail. 
 
Shooting range invitation: 
Although Mr. Marro could not attend the Sept. 9 Conservation Commission meeting, that 
evening he posted a public invitation to all 183 of his Facebook friends to come and shoot at his 
ﬁring range (attached). This strikes me as antagonistic, and will only increase the concerns of 
trail users’ public safety and the potential for conﬂict. The post was taken down four days later. 
 
Several trail users have told me privately that they question the legality of Mr. Marro’s gun 
range, and whether it meets the state’s required buﬀer from public trails and recreation land. I 
do not have any legal background, but I would urge the Conservation Commission to investigate 
this situation and work with Mr. Marro to ensure the public’s safety and keep the trail open. 
 
It is my hope that the city, Mr. Marro and trail users can work out positive solutions to 
encourage responsible trail usage, maintenance and monitoring in ways that respects the 
Morros’ peace and privacy, as well as the safety, recreation and trail access of all.
